description: A person who has told us about themselves and is not yet an employee. Nothing shipped means that, which is why this doctype exists; a Web Form onto Employee was refused, because a guest-writable Employee lets strangers consume the naming series and trips the absence-backfill trap.

fields.description: Terminal and irreversible once it leaves Invited or Submitted. Nothing here is reversible - a link cannot be revived.
fields.label: Status
fields.options:
Invited
Submitted
Made an employee
Expired
Cancelled

fields.description: Inside 078-PRIV-9's closed allow-list. Cleared when the submission is erased.
fields.label: Full name

fields.description: Who issued the link. Survives erasure - it holds no personal data about the joiner.
fields.label: Invited by
Signs in with
fields.description: The mobile number or email you already reached this person on. It is what they TYPE to sign in, and Frappe resolves a number through User.mobile_no. **HR's own entry, kept apart from the joiner's own answers on purpose**: putting it in the `mobile` column made HR's typing answer the question "has this joiner sent us anything yet?", so an empty form could be sent and marking the mobile number compulsory did nothing. Cleared when the details are erased.

The joiner's own sign-in. Set by "Make the sign-in" and never typed. The joining page resolves this row FROM the session through this field, so there is nothing a caller can post that reaches another person's row (079-SEC-4). Unique: one account is one submission. Deleted with the row when the details are erased.
fields.label: Sign-in

fields.description: When the joiner's access ends. Pressing Send does NOT end it (decision 4a) - somebody who finds their PAN card the next evening should not have to ring HR. The daily job closes the account on this date.
fields.label: Sign-in works until
Mobile number
fields.description: The number HR already reached this person on. It is also what they TYPE to sign in, resolved by Frappe through User.mobile_no. Inside the closed allow-list, so erasure clears it.

fields.label: Who to ring in an emergency

fields.description: Document types the joiner chose to bring rather than upload. Their words are never stored - only the type names they ticked.
fields.label: Bringing on the first day

fields.description: Set by HR AFTER creating the personnel record by hand. NEVER set by the form, and no joining date ever comes from it - a back-dated joining date makes Frappe mark the person Absent for every day since, and deleting those rows does not help.
fields.label: Employee

fields.description: The erase job skips a flagged row however old it is. Deleting something somebody has asked you to preserve is worse than keeping it too long.
fields.label: Legal hold
Cancelled because
fields.options:
By HR
The joiner is not coming
Sent to the wrong person
A newer sign-in was made
They were turned down
fields.description: Why the invite was closed. **Every reason gives the joiner the same answer on the page** (079-SEC-5): a different one for "turned down" would tell a candidate the outcome of their application through a web page instead of from their employer.

fields.label: Invite closed on
fields.description: When it stopped being live - cancelled, expired, or made an employee. The not-hired retention window runs from HERE and not from `modified`, because `modified` moves on ANY later edit: ticking legal hold and unticking it again would otherwise restart the clock.

fields.label: HR warned on
fields.description: Set once, so the daily job does not warn about the same row every day.
Which rule erased it: the not-hired window, the untouched backstop, HR's Purge, or because they became an employee.
